🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Supreme Court Upholds AMLO's Science Law: Public Research First</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court voted 7–1 to uphold the 2023 General Law on Humanities, Sciences, Technologies and Innovation, which opposition minorities in Congress had challenged. Public institutions keep priority in research funding. Researchers at private universities can still receive SNII stipends if they work with public institutions, for example by teaching, and focus on national priority areas set by Secihti. The lone dissent came from Justice Loretta Ortiz, who argued that the value of research is decided by "peers, not a secretariat, not an entity of the State."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Inside Mexico's Congress, Israel Named "Friendly Embassy of the Year"</u>

At the PRI's invitation, the evangelical group Policías Celestiales A.C. took over the Chamber of Deputies' Salón Legisladores to hand out its "Seguridad con Valor 2026" awards, organized with backing from Israel's embassy. Press attaché Dahlia Neumann collected the "friendly diplomatic mission of the year" prize on behalf of Ambassador Yoed Magen. The "mayors of the year": PAN's Giovanni Gutiérrez (Coyoacán) and Mauricio Tabe (Miguel Hidalgo), and PRI's David Sánchez Isidoro (Coacalco). The same day, people in Yucatán marched to demand an end to relations with Israel.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex Takes Back the Pump: 91% of Wholesale Gasoline</u>

Pemex's share of Mexico's wholesale gasoline market jumped from 79% to 91% so far this year, according to PetroIntelligence data reported by La Jornada. In diesel it holds 82%. The reason is price: in 2026, private resellers charged gas stations 4.86 pesos more per liter of regular, 1.11 more for premium and 2.07 more for diesel. The 2013 energy reform promised that competition would bring cheaper fuel. Instead, the public company is the cheap option.

🇲🇽🛢️ "President Trump, here there is a Constitution and here there are laws, so here oil rights cannot be given." "I tell him: 'Well, that's not true, President. Look at the results we have.' [...] Don't use Mexico. They have enough problems to solve over there." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 El Financiero asked whether Trump has sought Pemex assets in exchange for the trade deal. Sheinbaum said it has come up, "not in exchange," and the answer is always the Constitution. US firms can only work as Pemex contractors under the new Pemex law; Halliburton has done so for 80 years. On Trump's claim that cartels govern parts of Mexico, she cited fentanyl crossings down more than 60% and homicides cut in half. "They are campaigning and often want to use Mexico as part of their campaign." Their last call was on September 16.

🇲🇽⚖️ "He was very irresponsible, to say the least, not only for allowing foreign agents to take part in a ground operation against the law, but for the way they did it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 César Jáuregui, Chihuahua's former state prosecutor, has been arrested. The state prosecutor's office filed the first charges, for crimes by public servants; the Attorney General's Office (FGR) added treason. Chihuahua authorities named him the main person responsible for US agents joining a night raid on a drug lab in the Sierra Tarahumara, a task only the FGR may carry out. On a winding mountain road the vehicle overturned and two foreigners died. Mexican law does not allow ground operations by foreign agencies, and the Foreign Ministry was not informed.

🚨🇲🇽 "We are against any form of racism, and even more so when it comes to our compatriots in the United States. [...] For us, they are heroes." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 On Sunday another Mexican national died in a US immigration detention center. He had been detained in June; his family said he suffered from diabetes and hypertension and probably did not have all his medications. The Foreign Ministry contacted the family, issued a statement and will file a complaint in the United States, and consulates will reinforce protection of detainees' human rights. The question was about Los Tigres del Norte, whose song says "I didn't cross the border, the border crossed me." Sheinbaum hosted them at the National Palace, a first for a Mexican president. They turn 50 next year.

text: 🇲🇽🛢️ "Otherwise regular gasoline would be over 30 pesos and diesel over 35. Look at what is happening in various countries of the world." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 Mexico cut the tax on fuel and signed a voluntary agreement with gas station owners. Consumer agency Profeco reports an average diesel price of 26.98 pesos a liter, with 87.8% of stations under the 27-peso cap. Profeco is now inspecting stations selling premium at nearly 30 pesos, a 5-peso margin on fuel that also gets a tax stimulus. "The fiscal stimulus is for the people, not for the gas station owner to earn more money," said Profeco head Iván Escalante.
